summary: L002 executed successfully and passed the fixed G01 positive-Tc guard (8.5449 K <= 8.8322 K), but it did not improve the A05 incumbent. Pooled weighted OOF MAE was 7.8018 K versus 7.7526 K, a deterioration of 0.0492 K. Relative to A05, positive-Tc MAE worsened from 8.5051 K to 8.5449 K and reported-zero MAE worsened from 6.0806 K to 6.1508 K. High-Tc MAE improved slightly from 28.8502 K to 28.7654 K, showing a subgroup tradeoff rather than an eligible pooled win. On fe_anion specifically, hist_gradient_boosting/raw improved positive-Tc and high-Tc errors but worsened overall and reported-zero errors; the latter costs outweighed the gains. Thus neither a specialized hist_gradient_boosting/raw fe_anion expert nor the previously tested broad hist-gradient fallback improves A05.
next_focus: Retain A05 as the best guard-eligible development configuration: composition input, chemistry routing, extra_trees/raw global model, and extra_trees/raw experts for cu_o and other with fe_anion falling back globally. Any future work should evaluate A05 on a separately designed holdout or new data and, if development resumes, focus on richer ways to resolve the persistent cu_o zero-versus-high-Tc ambiguity rather than further combinations from this exhausted fixed menu.
stop_reason: The experiment budget is exhausted. The final focused untried fe_anion specialization was guard-eligible but failed to beat A05, leaving A05 at 7.7526 K pooled weighted OOF MAE as the incumbent. The available adaptive OOF evidence provides no eligible improvement from the tested estimator, target, input, and routing variants; further claims require independent evaluation rather than additional conclusions from these reused folds.
limitations: All measurements are adaptive development evidence from the same fixed-group training OOF folds, not independent validation or proof of generalization.
The chemistry routes are operational composition partitions, not verified physical material families.
The fe_anion route is small (285 rows, 37 groups), and its high-Tc subgroup has only 43 rows across 6 groups, so subgroup comparisons may be unstable.
Large cu_o errors persist: reported-zero materials are severely overpredicted while positive and high-Tc materials are often underpredicted.
No new superconductors can be inferred or claimed from these modeling results.
